issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
# The kernel's `publish` replaces the host's paths with placeholders

This round changes the kernel every world runs on (`src/hutian/`), not a domain; it is the first round of this world that does. The delivery repository's `dev` (2e787aa) is HuTian's `dev`: it holds the last round's pull request (#8, a paid step is done once), which the maintainer merged, and one small edit made after it. Base this round's work on that `dev`, from a branch of its own.

## What the host showed

1. On 2026-10-21 the six DojoWorld worlds published on `a-green-hand-jack/dojoworld-worlds` (`dw_ba784c2b0024`, `dw_42ca99b35e7d`, `dw_124d9fbd3a8e`, `dw_ed19e197a5df`, `dw_f414f11ec76e`, `dw_31f66e575aa1`) were written to a local directory with `dojoworld publish … --output DIR` at the default depth plus `release_assets`. 52 of the files written hold an absolute path of the host, 135 times in all. Five of the six worlds have some; `dw_124d9fbd3a8e` has none.
2. All 52 are contents of files in a position's repository (`<world>/blobs/<sha>`, the `repo_contents` facet): the status and configuration JSON of the worlds that position ran, which it committed (`runs/<name>/<world id>/status.json`, `status.txt`, `config.json`). The paths are the values of `receipts.directory` (46), `continues_home` (44) and the `read` list of a `world` resource (45). No other file had one: not the snapshot, the stream, the file listing, the release listing or the release files.
3. Every one of them begins with a directory the host holds for the world: its state root (`HUTIAN_HOME`; a world it ran lives under `<state root>/<world id>/worlds/<position>/<child world id>/`), or a state root its configuration gives a `world` resource in `read`. On this host all of them lie under the checkout the worlds were started from. Written with placeholders, they look like `<state root>/dw_…/worlds/<position>/rw_…/receipts` and `<a read state root>/rw_…/receipts`.
4. Public content may hold no absolute path of a machine (a rule of the repository). So these worlds are published without `repo_contents` and `repo_diffs`, and before each publish someone writes the site with `--output` and searches it by hand.
5. What `publish` checks today: every byte of every file it writes is compared with the world's own credential literals, and a hit refuses the publish and removes what was written (`publish.check`; USER 8.2). Nothing is done about the host's paths.
6. Disclosure is a whitelist projection (`observe/redact.py`, `observe/facets.py`): nothing reaches the output unless a granted facet copies it in by name. `repo_contents` copies a file's bytes as they are.
7. The three ways out share one export: `--dry-run` (`publish.dry_run`), `--output` (`publish.build`) and a push, once or with `--watch` (`publish_once` in `cli/main.py`). Each calls `publish.stage` and then `publish.check`.
8. Not every file of an export is written by it: release files and released pages are hard links to the host's copy of the record (`publish._link`, `_pages`), and a push hard-links the staged files into its copy of the data branch (`pages.sync`). DEV 20.2: nothing writes such a file in place, so a link never changes the original.
9. A blob is named by the git sha of its bytes, and `outputs.json` lists each file with that sha and size; a later publish, `--watch` included, reuses the last publish's blobs while a repository has not moved (`_outputs`, `previous`).
10. A PDF, a PNG or a release file (an archive, a video) can hold a path in a compressed or length-bound form. In these six worlds none did.
11. The publish regression tests are in `.agents/tests/test-stream.py` (`PublishOutputTests`, `PublishExportTests` and the publish classes after them). USER 8 and DEV 20 describe publishing.

## What to change

Change the kernel's `publish` so that in every file it writes (a dry run, `--output`, a push and `--watch` alike) the host's paths that belong to the world being published are replaced by readable placeholders, for example `<HUTIAN_HOME>/…`, and the dry run and the result say, for each world, how many were replaced. Which directories count, the placeholder each one gets, and what happens to a file that cannot be rewritten are yours to design; follow the whitelist projection that is already there, and say in the pull request what you chose and why. The world's record on the host stays as it is.

Keep the change small: the kernel's publish, regression tests that fail without the change and pass with it, and USER 8 and DEV 20 where they describe what changes (Chinese first, with the English copy in the same change). No domain definition changes. Write nothing of this case into the kernel: no host, user, directory name or world id.

## Where it goes

A new pull request to `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base `dev`, from a branch of its own. Merging is the maintainer's decision after review.

## How to try it

On `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there and run the repository's six regression suites there. Then run a fresh world of that version with a tiny task to its verified release: the smallest world that still shows each of its positions doing its part, Claude Code with `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort signed in with the OAuth token, at most 8 executions and 1200 model seconds. Something in that world must hold a host path for the replacement to act on (for instance a file a position commits that names the world's state root): a site with nothing to replace proves nothing.

With that version, run `publish --dry-run` and `publish --output DIR` on the trial world there, and show that the site holds no path of the trial machine's directories that belong to that world (search every file of it), and that the count the dry run reports equals the count in the `--output` result and the number of such paths the world's files held. Push nothing to a public repository from the trial machine.

## What the pull request says

What kernel code changed and why; the regression tests; which directories are replaced and by what, and how files that cannot be rewritten are treated; the trial world's id and its release; the search of the trial site (what was searched for and the counts) and the dry run's count against the result's.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages, and write no path of this host or of the trial machine there either.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
# HengWorld: a paid step is done once, by the owner of its function

The last two rounds made HengWorld and fixed it after review; the maintainer merged that pull request (#7). The delivery repository's `dev` now holds HengWorld as merged, with two small edits made since (the collaboration norm's paragraph on what the world supplies, and a comment in `organization.py`) and a fix to the kernel's gateway. Base this round's work on that `dev`.

HengWorld has since run for real on its host, twice. The second world, `hw_bd6dcbfd7f6b`, continued the first with a paid `http` resource: a Google Gemini model behind the gateway, used by CrewCut's describe step (a vision-language model drafting the description of each shot of a film) and its continuity judge. What it showed:

1. The world made 264 requests to the paid resource. About 44 were needed: 37 shot descriptions, the judge on the 3 shots of the one evaluated run, and a few probes. The task maker's own reproduction script counts the same.
2. The same 37 descriptions were drafted three times, by three positions: the task maker (51 requests, describe and judge), the scorer (135: its own describe, the judge, a control of the judge on 74 shots, 10 failed attempts, probes) and the executor (78: two full describe passes, the first cut short). The auditor made none: it reused the judge's results and recomputed.
3. The three drafts differ: the describe step sets no temperature, so the two drafts the task maker kept differ in all 37 texts. Its decision record D10 had to choose which draft the answer key carries; a later step has no way to know which one to use unless one position made it and published it.
4. The duplication came before anyone owned the step. Every position took up the new objective at once; the work assignment named the owner of the Gemini calls only later (steward#8), and the executor's record says its 76 requests were made before that assignment and duplicate the task maker's.
5. That world cost under one dollar. A full run of the benchmark it serves has about 9,716 shots, and paid generators and a judge on top: the same step three times is three times the cost and three answers.

Evidence: the world's public page (https://a-green-hand-jack.github.io/hengworld-worlds/#/w/hw_bd6dcbfd7f6b), its release record `record/decisions/D10-two-description-drafts.json`, the executor's `runs/round2/README.md` and the scorer's `scores/spend/spend.json`.

## What to change

Nothing in HengWorld tells a position that a step which costs money or uses up a quota (generating, scoring or judging with a paid resource) belongs to one function. Change HengWorld's definition (function texts, norms or guides) so that each position knows:

- such a step is done once, by the position that holds the function it belongs to, and its result is published together with the model and the settings used;
- a position that needs that result reads the published one; to check it, it samples, or says why the whole step must be redone, rather than redoing it by default;
- the audit may still rerun such a step to reproduce it, and its record says what it reran and what that cost.

Fact 4 is the one to answer: every position starts on a new objective at once, so a position must know from the start, from the definition itself, which function such a step belongs to, not only once a work assignment arrives; and the other positions make no request to the paid resource for that step before its result is published. The wording is yours.

Say functions, never positions: where a text must say who, use the owner slots (`{{ owners.* }}`). Keep each change small: a sentence or two where the subject already is, not a new section of rules. Write nothing of this world's case into the domain: no model, provider, film, benchmark or price. Change nothing else. If a document describes what you change, change it too, Chinese first with the English copy in the same change.

## Where it goes

A new pull request to `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base `dev`, from a branch of its own. Merging is the maintainer's decision after review.

## How to try it

On `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there, run the repository's six regression suites there, and run a fresh HengWorld world to its release with a small task that uses a paid resource. Give that world an `http` resource for Gemini: upstream `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai`, `credential_env` `GEMINI_API_KEY` (set on the trial machine for `ht-resource run` commands), model `gemini-3.8-flash`, `limits.max_requests` 150. The task, from CrewCut's files (copied there as in the last trials):

- Corpus: Caminandes 3 as CrewCut's published dataset (revision d509bed) gives it, with the pinned master verified by its checksum; the copy of the master only if the pinned file cannot be fetched. No Breakdown rebuild.
- Shot descriptions of all 37 shots with CrewCut's describe step, published with the model and settings used.
- One run: `caminandes3-L1-0000-scr` with the fixed pipeline, smoke profile; c completed with the judge's shot correspondence from those descriptions. Any check of the judge itself stays small (at most 10 shots per control).
- Known from the last world: with this model, CrewCut's describe and judge get an empty reply at their own `max_tokens`; it worked with `reasoning_effort` `none` and the judge's `max_tokens` at least 128.
- Every request to Gemini is recorded with its position and purpose.

The trial world's workers are Claude Code with `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token, with at most 40 executions and 2400 model seconds.

The Gemini key cannot be revoked on its own: as soon as the trial world has reached its release and its records are taken, stop it (`stop`, or `finish`), and leave no command on the trial machine that holds the key.

## What the pull request says

What texts changed and why; the trial world's id and its release; the requests to the paid resource by position and purpose (from the trial world's own records), set against what the steps needed: each paid step made by one position only, any rerun by the audit stated with its count; the limit (150) and whether it was reached: if it was, the count proves nothing and the pull request says so; and how this compares with the 264 of `hw_bd6dcbfd7f6b`.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages.

issue.body:
# Improve HengWorld from the review of its pull request

The last round made HengWorld: its pull request, #7 to `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian` (branch `hengworld`, base `dev`), and its trial, world `hw_f54caea55d2a` on `trial-machine`, reached a release. The maintainer's review of #7 found the following. This round fixes them in the same pull request.

What the review found:

1. The position name `runner` is a word the kernel already uses. The kernel's time stream records the host side of a world (the driver, claims, sandboxes) as the stream and actor `runner` (`src/hutian/hutian/observe/stream.py`, `src/hutian/hutian/execution/session.py`), and an entry without a role is shown by its actor. So in a HengWorld world an entry such as "world runner driver ended: world-complete" cannot be told apart from the position's own entries. The role-name check in `.agents/tests/test-coordination.py` does not catch it: it counts the names of each definition only in that definition's files. DojoWorld met the same collision and renamed its position to `sparring-partner`.
2. The function texts (`src/hengworld/hengworld/instructions/1-function/*.md.j2`) name other positions (steward, task-maker, runner, scorer, auditor) and repeat what the organization part of the instruction already tells each position: read tiers, who supplies whom, the kernel position a role holds. A function text says what the work is and the standard it is held to; who does what reaches each position through the organization part (DEV 15.3: one kind of information per file). When a world has fewer positions, a function falls to another position and the names written into it are wrong. KaiTianWorld's and DojoWorld's function texts are one paragraph each and name no position; where a norm or guide has to say who, it uses the owner slots (`{{ owners.* }}`).
3. Conditions of the last round were written as rules of the domain. `5-norms/collaboration.md.j2` says that keys for models, generators or judges are not supplied, and the runner's function text says there are no such keys. What a world has comes from its resources, and a world that runs CrewCut's Issue #3 for real will have those keys, so these sentences would mislead its workers. Of the same kind: "Do not paste private code … into issues or messages that are public" in the norms comes from this KaiTianWorld world's public page, not from HengWorld; "the objective names a fallback copy" in the curator's function text comes from the last trial's objective. What one world has, or may not do, reaches it through its objective and its resources.
4. The two CI lines (`docker build … -f src/hengworld/Dockerfile …` in `.github/workflows/candidate.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`) are in the pull request's text, not in its changes: the delivery token could not write `.github/workflows/`. The maintainer has since given it that permission: put them in the pull request.
5. The comment of the organization graph (`assets/hengworld-graph.mmd` and its English copy) says that only task-maker and scorer hold the reference answers; the auditor reads them too, as the instructions correctly say.

Change HengWorld (its definition, instruction texts, graphs and documents, Chinese first with the English copies in the same change) so that the pull request no longer has these, and nothing else. Change nothing that only a worker did. Keep each change small; a renamed position is renamed everywhere it appears (definition, instruction files, both graphs, README and USER in both languages, the per-domain checks).

Where it goes: the same pull request, #7. Push new commits to its branch `hengworld` and update its text; do not open another. Merging is the maintainer's decision after review.

How to try it: as in the last round. On `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there, run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh HengWorld world to its release with the same small task, a short piece of each CrewCut pipeline:

- Breakdown: the dev film Caminandes 3 (2.5 minutes, 37 shots, no dialogue), from the catalogue query to its task packages, compared with the published dataset (cuts, dialogue, hierarchy, task ids), with each difference listed and explained; use the copy of the pinned master only when the pinned file cannot be fetched, and record that;
- Evaluation: one of those tasks run with the fixed pipeline and the placeholder generator, scored up to the delivery check and cut F1.

CrewCut reaches the trial machine as a git bundle copied over ssh, and the other files of the `crewcut` resource the same way. The trial needs no key for a generator, a vision-language model or a judge; what needs one (shot descriptions, the judge, real generators, screening) is not run, and the record says so. The trial world's workers are Claude Code with the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token, with at most 30 executions and 2400 model seconds.

What the pull request says: what was made, what this round changed, and how the new trial ended: the trial world's id, its release, the results of both pieces compared with the last trial's, and what was not run.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages.

# HengWorld: a world that builds a benchmark and evaluates systems on it

Make a new domain for HuTian: HengWorld (衡, "to weigh"). Building a benchmark is making a scale; evaluating systems is weighing them on it. Its first user is CrewCut, a benchmark of film production by agent systems, but the domain is general: a later world could build, say, a software benchmark with it.

What to make:

- A domain package `hengworld` (command `hengworld`, world id prefix `hw`) beside the five domains under `src/`, equal to them and added the way `DEV.md` says a domain is added: its definition through the `hutian.definitions` entry point, its organization graph in `assets/` in Chinese and English, its system and worker images, its default resources, its place in `install.sh`, the CI workflows and the per-domain checks, and its sections in README and USER, Chinese first with the English copies in the same change.
- The positions, edges, read tiers, functions and release gate are not given here. Design them from the real division of the work of building a benchmark and evaluating systems under one set of rules, and give the reason for each.
- No special cases: nothing in the definition names CrewCut, films or a catalogue. What a benchmark needs comes into a HengWorld world through its objective and the benchmark's own documents.
- The shape of the work, as CrewCut decided for its own pipelines: what needs judgment (finding candidates, reading licences, telling the work from its extras, choosing the file to pin, what to do after a failure, organizing runs) is done by agents; the benchmark's commands are reproducible steps and checks of whether each step succeeded; every decision is recorded as data, so that anyone can reproduce the result from the record without repeating the judgment.
- Keep it small: the positions, their contracts and the release gate make a world, not features.

CrewCut, read only: the `crewcut` resource holds a bare mirror of CrewCut's `dev` (df54b3a), its Issue #3, which says what its two pipelines must do and deliver, the published dataset at revision d509bed, and a copy of the pinned master of Caminandes 3. Read its README.md, `.agents/memory/project/agentic-pipelines.md` and Issue #3. Nothing goes back to CrewCut. CrewCut's open decisions (the vision-language model, the generators and their prices, the judge model, the scale of the official runs, the raters) belong to its maintainer: do not make them.

Where it goes: one pull request to the private repository `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base branch `dev`, which holds HuTian's code. Merging it is the maintainer's decision after review.

How to try it: on `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there, run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh HengWorld world to its release with a small task that covers a short piece of each CrewCut pipeline:

- Breakdown: the dev film Caminandes 3 (2.5 minutes, 37 shots, no dialogue), from the catalogue query to its task packages, compared with the published dataset (cuts, dialogue, hierarchy, task ids), with each difference listed and explained; use the copy of the pinned master only when the pinned file cannot be fetched, and record that;
- Evaluation: one of those tasks run with the fixed pipeline and the placeholder generator, scored up to the delivery check and cut F1.

CrewCut reaches the trial machine as a git bundle copied over ssh, and the other files of the `crewcut` resource the same way. The trial needs no key for a generator, a vision-language model or a judge; what needs one (shot descriptions, the judge, real generators, screening) is not run, and the record says so. The trial world's workers are Claude Code with the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token, with at most 20 executions and 2400 model seconds.

What the pull request says: what was made, and how the trial ended: the trial world's id, its release, the results of both pieces, and what was not run.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages.

# The kernel's `publish` replaces the host's paths with placeholders

This round changes the kernel every world runs on (`src/hutian/`), not a domain; it is the first round of this world that does. The delivery repository's `dev` (2e787aa) is HuTian's `dev`: it holds the last round's pull request (#8, a paid step is done once), which the maintainer merged, and one small edit made after it. Base this round's work on that `dev`, from a branch of its own.

## What the host showed

1. On 2026-10-21 the six DojoWorld worlds published on `a-green-hand-jack/dojoworld-worlds` (`dw_ba784c2b0024`, `dw_42ca99b35e7d`, `dw_124d9fbd3a8e`, `dw_ed19e197a5df`, `dw_f414f11ec76e`, `dw_31f66e575aa1`) were written to a local directory with `dojoworld publish … --output DIR` at the default depth plus `release_assets`. 52 of the files written hold an absolute path of the host, 135 times in all. Five of the six worlds have some; `dw_124d9fbd3a8e` has none.
2. All 52 are contents of files in a position's repository (`<world>/blobs/<sha>`, the `repo_contents` facet): the status and configuration JSON of the worlds that position ran, which it committed (`runs/<name>/<world id>/status.json`, `status.txt`, `config.json`). The paths are the values of `receipts.directory` (46), `continues_home` (44) and the `read` list of a `world` resource (45). No other file had one: not the snapshot, the stream, the file listing, the release listing or the release files.
3. Every one of them begins with a directory the host holds for the world: its state root (`HUTIAN_HOME`; a world it ran lives under `<state root>/<world id>/worlds/<position>/<child world id>/`), or a state root its configuration gives a `world` resource in `read`. On this host all of them lie under the checkout the worlds were started from. Written with placeholders, they look like `<state root>/dw_…/worlds/<position>/rw_…/receipts` and `<a read state root>/rw_…/receipts`.
4. Public content may hold no absolute path of a machine (a rule of the repository). So these worlds are published without `repo_contents` and `repo_diffs`, and before each publish someone writes the site with `--output` and searches it by hand.
5. What `publish` checks today: every byte of every file it writes is compared with the world's own credential literals, and a hit refuses the publish and removes what was written (`publish.check`; USER 8.2). Nothing is done about the host's paths.
6. Disclosure is a whitelist projection (`observe/redact.py`, `observe/facets.py`): nothing reaches the output unless a granted facet copies it in by name. `repo_contents` copies a file's bytes as they are.
7. The three ways out share one export: `--dry-run` (`publish.dry_run`), `--output` (`publish.build`) and a push, once or with `--watch` (`publish_once` in `cli/main.py`). Each calls `publish.stage` and then `publish.check`.
8. Not every file of an export is written by it: release files and released pages are hard links to the host's copy of the record (`publish._link`, `_pages`), and a push hard-links the staged files into its copy of the data branch (`pages.sync`). DEV 20.2: nothing writes such a file in place, so a link never changes the original.
9. A blob is named by the git sha of its bytes, and `outputs.json` lists each file with that sha and size; a later publish, `--watch` included, reuses the last publish's blobs while a repository has not moved (`_outputs`, `previous`).
10. A PDF, a PNG or a release file (an archive, a video) can hold a path in a compressed or length-bound form. In these six worlds none did.
11. The publish regression tests are in `.agents/tests/test-stream.py` (`PublishOutputTests`, `PublishExportTests` and the publish classes after them). USER 8 and DEV 20 describe publishing.

## What to change

Change the kernel's `publish` so that in every file it writes (a dry run, `--output`, a push and `--watch` alike) the host's paths that belong to the world being published are replaced by readable placeholders, for example `<HUTIAN_HOME>/…`, and the dry run and the result say, for each world, how many were replaced. Which directories count, the placeholder each one gets, and what happens to a file that cannot be rewritten are yours to design; follow the whitelist projection that is already there, and say in the pull request what you chose and why. The world's record on the host stays as it is.

Keep the change small: the kernel's publish, regression tests that fail without the change and pass with it, and USER 8 and DEV 20 where they describe what changes (Chinese first, with the English copy in the same change). No domain definition changes. Write nothing of this case into the kernel: no host, user, directory name or world id.

## Where it goes

A new pull request to `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base `dev`, from a branch of its own. Merging is the maintainer's decision after review.

## How to try it

On `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there and run the repository's six regression suites there. Then run a fresh world of that version with a tiny task to its verified release: the smallest world that still shows each of its positions doing its part, Claude Code with `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort signed in with the OAuth token, at most 8 executions and 1200 model seconds. Something in that world must hold a host path for the replacement to act on (for instance a file a position commits that names the world's state root): a site with nothing to replace proves nothing.

With that version, run `publish --dry-run` and `publish --output DIR` on the trial world there, and show that the site holds no path of the trial machine's directories that belong to that world (search every file of it), and that the count the dry run reports equals the count in the `--output` result and the number of such paths the world's files held. Push nothing to a public repository from the trial machine.

## What the pull request says

What kernel code changed and why; the regression tests; which directories are replaced and by what, and how files that cannot be rewritten are treated; the trial world's id and its release; the search of the trial site (what was searched for and the counts) and the dry run's count against the result's.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages, and write no path of this host or of the trial machine there either.

issue.body:
# HengWorld: a paid step is done once, by the owner of its function

The last two rounds made HengWorld and fixed it after review; the maintainer merged that pull request (#7). The delivery repository's `dev` now holds HengWorld as merged, with two small edits made since (the collaboration norm's paragraph on what the world supplies, and a comment in `organization.py`) and a fix to the kernel's gateway. Base this round's work on that `dev`.

HengWorld has since run for real on its host, twice. The second world, `hw_bd6dcbfd7f6b`, continued the first with a paid `http` resource: a Google Gemini model behind the gateway, used by CrewCut's describe step (a vision-language model drafting the description of each shot of a film) and its continuity judge. What it showed:

1. The world made 264 requests to the paid resource. About 44 were needed: 37 shot descriptions, the judge on the 3 shots of the one evaluated run, and a few probes. The task maker's own reproduction script counts the same.
2. The same 37 descriptions were drafted three times, by three positions: the task maker (51 requests, describe and judge), the scorer (135: its own describe, the judge, a control of the judge on 74 shots, 10 failed attempts, probes) and the executor (78: two full describe passes, the first cut short). The auditor made none: it reused the judge's results and recomputed.
3. The three drafts differ: the describe step sets no temperature, so the two drafts the task maker kept differ in all 37 texts. Its decision record D10 had to choose which draft the answer key carries; a later step has no way to know which one to use unless one position made it and published it.
4. The duplication came before anyone owned the step. Every position took up the new objective at once; the work assignment named the owner of the Gemini calls only later (steward#8), and the executor's record says its 76 requests were made before that assignment and duplicate the task maker's.
5. That world cost under one dollar. A full run of the benchmark it serves has about 9,716 shots, and paid generators and a judge on top: the same step three times is three times the cost and three answers.

Evidence: the world's public page (https://a-green-hand-jack.github.io/hengworld-worlds/#/w/hw_bd6dcbfd7f6b), its release record `record/decisions/D10-two-description-drafts.json`, the executor's `runs/round2/README.md` and the scorer's `scores/spend/spend.json`.

## What to change

Nothing in HengWorld tells a position that a step which costs money or uses up a quota (generating, scoring or judging with a paid resource) belongs to one function. Change HengWorld's definition (function texts, norms or guides) so that each position knows:

- such a step is done once, by the position that holds the function it belongs to, and its result is published together with the model and the settings used;
- a position that needs that result reads the published one; to check it, it samples, or says why the whole step must be redone, rather than redoing it by default;
- the audit may still rerun such a step to reproduce it, and its record says what it reran and what that cost.

Fact 4 is the one to answer: every position starts on a new objective at once, so a position must know from the start, from the definition itself, which function such a step belongs to, not only once a work assignment arrives; and the other positions make no request to the paid resource for that step before its result is published. The wording is yours.

Say functions, never positions: where a text must say who, use the owner slots (`{{ owners.* }}`). Keep each change small: a sentence or two where the subject already is, not a new section of rules. Write nothing of this world's case into the domain: no model, provider, film, benchmark or price. Change nothing else. If a document describes what you change, change it too, Chinese first with the English copy in the same change.

## Where it goes

A new pull request to `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base `dev`, from a branch of its own. Merging is the maintainer's decision after review.

## How to try it

On `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there, run the repository's six regression suites there, and run a fresh HengWorld world to its release with a small task that uses a paid resource. Give that world an `http` resource for Gemini: upstream `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai`, `credential_env` `GEMINI_API_KEY` (set on the trial machine for `ht-resource run` commands), model `gemini-3.8-flash`, `limits.max_requests` 150. The task, from CrewCut's files (copied there as in the last trials):

- Corpus: Caminandes 3 as CrewCut's published dataset (revision d509bed) gives it, with the pinned master verified by its checksum; the copy of the master only if the pinned file cannot be fetched. No Breakdown rebuild.
- Shot descriptions of all 37 shots with CrewCut's describe step, published with the model and settings used.
- One run: `caminandes3-L1-0000-scr` with the fixed pipeline, smoke profile; c completed with the judge's shot correspondence from those descriptions. Any check of the judge itself stays small (at most 10 shots per control).
- Known from the last world: with this model, CrewCut's describe and judge get an empty reply at their own `max_tokens`; it worked with `reasoning_effort` `none` and the judge's `max_tokens` at least 128.
- Every request to Gemini is recorded with its position and purpose.

The trial world's workers are Claude Code with `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token, with at most 40 executions and 2400 model seconds.

The Gemini key cannot be revoked on its own: as soon as the trial world has reached its release and its records are taken, stop it (`stop`, or `finish`), and leave no command on the trial machine that holds the key.

## What the pull request says

What texts changed and why; the trial world's id and its release; the requests to the paid resource by position and purpose (from the trial world's own records), set against what the steps needed: each paid step made by one position only, any rerun by the audit stated with its count; the limit (150) and whether it was reached: if it was, the count proves nothing and the pull request says so; and how this compares with the 264 of `hw_bd6dcbfd7f6b`.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages.

issue.body:
# Improve HengWorld from the review of its pull request

The last round made HengWorld: its pull request, #7 to `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian` (branch `hengworld`, base `dev`), and its trial, world `hw_f54caea55d2a` on `trial-machine`, reached a release. The maintainer's review of #7 found the following. This round fixes them in the same pull request.

What the review found:

1. The position name `runner` is a word the kernel already uses. The kernel's time stream records the host side of a world (the driver, claims, sandboxes) as the stream and actor `runner` (`src/hutian/hutian/observe/stream.py`, `src/hutian/hutian/execution/session.py`), and an entry without a role is shown by its actor. So in a HengWorld world an entry such as "world runner driver ended: world-complete" cannot be told apart from the position's own entries. The role-name check in `.agents/tests/test-coordination.py` does not catch it: it counts the names of each definition only in that definition's files. DojoWorld met the same collision and renamed its position to `sparring-partner`.
2. The function texts (`src/hengworld/hengworld/instructions/1-function/*.md.j2`) name other positions (steward, task-maker, runner, scorer, auditor) and repeat what the organization part of the instruction already tells each position: read tiers, who supplies whom, the kernel position a role holds. A function text says what the work is and the standard it is held to; who does what reaches each position through the organization part (DEV 15.3: one kind of information per file). When a world has fewer positions, a function falls to another position and the names written into it are wrong. KaiTianWorld's and DojoWorld's function texts are one paragraph each and name no position; where a norm or guide has to say who, it uses the owner slots (`{{ owners.* }}`).
3. Conditions of the last round were written as rules of the domain. `5-norms/collaboration.md.j2` says that keys for models, generators or judges are not supplied, and the runner's function text says there are no such keys. What a world has comes from its resources, and a world that runs CrewCut's Issue #3 for real will have those keys, so these sentences would mislead its workers. Of the same kind: "Do not paste private code … into issues or messages that are public" in the norms comes from this KaiTianWorld world's public page, not from HengWorld; "the objective names a fallback copy" in the curator's function text comes from the last trial's objective. What one world has, or may not do, reaches it through its objective and its resources.
4. The two CI lines (`docker build … -f src/hengworld/Dockerfile …` in `.github/workflows/candidate.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`) are in the pull request's text, not in its changes: the delivery token could not write `.github/workflows/`. The maintainer has since given it that permission: put them in the pull request.
5. The comment of the organization graph (`assets/hengworld-graph.mmd` and its English copy) says that only task-maker and scorer hold the reference answers; the auditor reads them too, as the instructions correctly say.

Change HengWorld (its definition, instruction texts, graphs and documents, Chinese first with the English copies in the same change) so that the pull request no longer has these, and nothing else. Change nothing that only a worker did. Keep each change small; a renamed position is renamed everywhere it appears (definition, instruction files, both graphs, README and USER in both languages, the per-domain checks).

Where it goes: the same pull request, #7. Push new commits to its branch `hengworld` and update its text; do not open another. Merging is the maintainer's decision after review.

How to try it: as in the last round. On `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there, run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh HengWorld world to its release with the same small task, a short piece of each CrewCut pipeline:

- Breakdown: the dev film Caminandes 3 (2.5 minutes, 37 shots, no dialogue), from the catalogue query to its task packages, compared with the published dataset (cuts, dialogue, hierarchy, task ids), with each difference listed and explained; use the copy of the pinned master only when the pinned file cannot be fetched, and record that;
- Evaluation: one of those tasks run with the fixed pipeline and the placeholder generator, scored up to the delivery check and cut F1.

CrewCut reaches the trial machine as a git bundle copied over ssh, and the other files of the `crewcut` resource the same way. The trial needs no key for a generator, a vision-language model or a judge; what needs one (shot descriptions, the judge, real generators, screening) is not run, and the record says so. The trial world's workers are Claude Code with the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token, with at most 30 executions and 2400 model seconds.

What the pull request says: what was made, what this round changed, and how the new trial ended: the trial world's id, its release, the results of both pieces compared with the last trial's, and what was not run.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages.

issue.author: analyst
issue.body: Evidence: world/operator trials/v0.1.0/RECORD.md @061dc4213c3c step 4-5. Six positions; drive 1 ended budget-exhausted at 20/20 executions, 793/2400 model s, auditor approval still pending; 4 more executions after raising to 40 verified it. Not a package defect (the domain sets no default budget). Need: either an organization/edge design that reaches release in fewer wake-ups (fewer comment round trips, fewer positions woken per step), or a stated expected execution count in the organization docs and a note for the PR. Fixed when a fresh trial reaches verified within 20 executions, or the PR states the need.
issue.title: Trial hw_f54caea55d2a needed 24 executions; the 20-execution limit ended it unverified

comments.author: architect
comments.body: Design answer (organization.md, 'Expected execution count'): floor ~7, realistic ~20-25 for a two-pipeline task; we keep six positions because merging runner/scorer or auditor into a maker removes the independence the gate relies on. Recommended: >=30 executions for a task of this size, and the PR states that the 20-execution limit ended drive 1 and 4 more executions at limit 40 reached verification. Operator/builder: please carry that note into the PR text.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
# HengWorld: a world that builds a benchmark and evaluates systems on it

Make a new domain for HuTian: HengWorld (衡, "to weigh"). Building a benchmark is making a scale; evaluating systems is weighing them on it. Its first user is CrewCut, a benchmark of film production by agent systems, but the domain is general: a later world could build, say, a software benchmark with it.

What to make:

- A domain package `hengworld` (command `hengworld`, world id prefix `hw`) beside the five domains under `src/`, equal to them and added the way `DEV.md` says a domain is added: its definition through the `hutian.definitions` entry point, its organization graph in `assets/` in Chinese and English, its system and worker images, its default resources, its place in `install.sh`, the CI workflows and the per-domain checks, and its sections in README and USER, Chinese first with the English copies in the same change.
- The positions, edges, read tiers, functions and release gate are not given here. Design them from the real division of the work of building a benchmark and evaluating systems under one set of rules, and give the reason for each.
- No special cases: nothing in the definition names CrewCut, films or a catalogue. What a benchmark needs comes into a HengWorld world through its objective and the benchmark's own documents.
- The shape of the work, as CrewCut decided for its own pipelines: what needs judgment (finding candidates, reading licences, telling the work from its extras, choosing the file to pin, what to do after a failure, organizing runs) is done by agents; the benchmark's commands are reproducible steps and checks of whether each step succeeded; every decision is recorded as data, so that anyone can reproduce the result from the record without repeating the judgment.
- Keep it small: the positions, their contracts and the release gate make a world, not features.

CrewCut, read only: the `crewcut` resource holds a bare mirror of CrewCut's `dev` (df54b3a), its Issue #3, which says what its two pipelines must do and deliver, the published dataset at revision d509bed, and a copy of the pinned master of Caminandes 3. Read its README.md, `.agents/memory/project/agentic-pipelines.md` and Issue #3. Nothing goes back to CrewCut. CrewCut's open decisions (the vision-language model, the generators and their prices, the judge model, the scale of the official runs, the raters) belong to its maintainer: do not make them.

Where it goes: one pull request to the private repository `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base branch `dev`, which holds HuTian's code. Merging it is the maintainer's decision after review.

How to try it: on `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there, run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh HengWorld world to its release with a small task that covers a short piece of each CrewCut pipeline:

- Breakdown: the dev film Caminandes 3 (2.5 minutes, 37 shots, no dialogue), from the catalogue query to its task packages, compared with the published dataset (cuts, dialogue, hierarchy, task ids), with each difference listed and explained; use the copy of the pinned master only when the pinned file cannot be fetched, and record that;
- Evaluation: one of those tasks run with the fixed pipeline and the placeholder generator, scored up to the delivery check and cut F1.

CrewCut reaches the trial machine as a git bundle copied over ssh, and the other files of the `crewcut` resource the same way. The trial needs no key for a generator, a vision-language model or a judge; what needs one (shot descriptions, the judge, real generators, screening) is not run, and the record says so. The trial world's workers are Claude Code with the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token, with at most 20 executions and 2400 model seconds.

What the pull request says: what was made, and how the trial ended: the trial world's id, its release, the results of both pieces, and what was not run.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
# The kernel's `publish` replaces the host's paths with placeholders

This round changes the kernel every world runs on (`src/hutian/`), not a domain; it is the first round of this world that does. The delivery repository's `dev` (2e787aa) is HuTian's `dev`: it holds the last round's pull request (#8, a paid step is done once), which the maintainer merged, and one small edit made after it. Base this round's work on that `dev`, from a branch of its own.

## What the host showed

1. On 2026-10-21 the six DojoWorld worlds published on `a-green-hand-jack/dojoworld-worlds` (`dw_ba784c2b0024`, `dw_42ca99b35e7d`, `dw_124d9fbd3a8e`, `dw_ed19e197a5df`, `dw_f414f11ec76e`, `dw_31f66e575aa1`) were written to a local directory with `dojoworld publish … --output DIR` at the default depth plus `release_assets`. 52 of the files written hold an absolute path of the host, 135 times in all. Five of the six worlds have some; `dw_124d9fbd3a8e` has none.
2. All 52 are contents of files in a position's repository (`<world>/blobs/<sha>`, the `repo_contents` facet): the status and configuration JSON of the worlds that position ran, which it committed (`runs/<name>/<world id>/status.json`, `status.txt`, `config.json`). The paths are the values of `receipts.directory` (46), `continues_home` (44) and the `read` list of a `world` resource (45). No other file had one: not the snapshot, the stream, the file listing, the release listing or the release files.
3. Every one of them begins with a directory the host holds for the world: its state root (`HUTIAN_HOME`; a world it ran lives under `<state root>/<world id>/worlds/<position>/<child world id>/`), or a state root its configuration gives a `world` resource in `read`. On this host all of them lie under the checkout the worlds were started from. Written with placeholders, they look like `<state root>/dw_…/worlds/<position>/rw_…/receipts` and `<a read state root>/rw_…/receipts`.
4. Public content may hold no absolute path of a machine (a rule of the repository). So these worlds are published without `repo_contents` and `repo_diffs`, and before each publish someone writes the site with `--output` and searches it by hand.
5. What `publish` checks today: every byte of every file it writes is compared with the world's own credential literals, and a hit refuses the publish and removes what was written (`publish.check`; USER 8.2). Nothing is done about the host's paths.
6. Disclosure is a whitelist projection (`observe/redact.py`, `observe/facets.py`): nothing reaches the output unless a granted facet copies it in by name. `repo_contents` copies a file's bytes as they are.
7. The three ways out share one export: `--dry-run` (`publish.dry_run`), `--output` (`publish.build`) and a push, once or with `--watch` (`publish_once` in `cli/main.py`). Each calls `publish.stage` and then `publish.check`.
8. Not every file of an export is written by it: release files and released pages are hard links to the host's copy of the record (`publish._link`, `_pages`), and a push hard-links the staged files into its copy of the data branch (`pages.sync`). DEV 20.2: nothing writes such a file in place, so a link never changes the original.
9. A blob is named by the git sha of its bytes, and `outputs.json` lists each file with that sha and size; a later publish, `--watch` included, reuses the last publish's blobs while a repository has not moved (`_outputs`, `previous`).
10. A PDF, a PNG or a release file (an archive, a video) can hold a path in a compressed or length-bound form. In these six worlds none did.
11. The publish regression tests are in `.agents/tests/test-stream.py` (`PublishOutputTests`, `PublishExportTests` and the publish classes after them). USER 8 and DEV 20 describe publishing.

## What to change

Change the kernel's `publish` so that in every file it writes (a dry run, `--output`, a push and `--watch` alike) the host's paths that belong to the world being published are replaced by readable placeholders, for example `<HUTIAN_HOME>/…`, and the dry run and the result say, for each world, how many were replaced. Which directories count, the placeholder each one gets, and what happens to a file that cannot be rewritten are yours to design; follow the whitelist projection that is already there, and say in the pull request what you chose and why. The world's record on the host stays as it is.

Keep the change small: the kernel's publish, regression tests that fail without the change and pass with it, and USER 8 and DEV 20 where they describe what changes (Chinese first, with the English copy in the same change). No domain definition changes. Write nothing of this case into the kernel: no host, user, directory name or world id.

## Where it goes

A new pull request to `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base `dev`, from a branch of its own. Merging is the maintainer's decision after review.

## How to try it

On `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there and run the repository's six regression suites there. Then run a fresh world of that version with a tiny task to its verified release: the smallest world that still shows each of its positions doing its part, Claude Code with `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort signed in with the OAuth token, at most 8 executions and 1200 model seconds. Something in that world must hold a host path for the replacement to act on (for instance a file a position commits that names the world's state root): a site with nothing to replace proves nothing.

With that version, run `publish --dry-run` and `publish --output DIR` on the trial world there, and show that the site holds no path of the trial machine's directories that belong to that world (search every file of it), and that the count the dry run reports equals the count in the `--output` result and the number of such paths the world's files held. Push nothing to a public repository from the trial machine.

## What the pull request says

What kernel code changed and why; the regression tests; which directories are replaced and by what, and how files that cannot be rewritten are treated; the trial world's id and its release; the search of the trial site (what was searched for and the counts) and the dry run's count against the result's.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages, and write no path of this host or of the trial machine there either.

# HengWorld: a paid step is done once, by the owner of its function

The last two rounds made HengWorld and fixed it after review; the maintainer merged that pull request (#7). The delivery repository's `dev` now holds HengWorld as merged, with two small edits made since (the collaboration norm's paragraph on what the world supplies, and a comment in `organization.py`) and a fix to the kernel's gateway. Base this round's work on that `dev`.

HengWorld has since run for real on its host, twice. The second world, `hw_bd6dcbfd7f6b`, continued the first with a paid `http` resource: a Google Gemini model behind the gateway, used by CrewCut's describe step (a vision-language model drafting the description of each shot of a film) and its continuity judge. What it showed:

1. The world made 264 requests to the paid resource. About 44 were needed: 37 shot descriptions, the judge on the 3 shots of the one evaluated run, and a few probes. The task maker's own reproduction script counts the same.
2. The same 37 descriptions were drafted three times, by three positions: the task maker (51 requests, describe and judge), the scorer (135: its own describe, the judge, a control of the judge on 74 shots, 10 failed attempts, probes) and the executor (78: two full describe passes, the first cut short). The auditor made none: it reused the judge's results and recomputed.
3. The three drafts differ: the describe step sets no temperature, so the two drafts the task maker kept differ in all 37 texts. Its decision record D10 had to choose which draft the answer key carries; a later step has no way to know which one to use unless one position made it and published it.
4. The duplication came before anyone owned the step. Every position took up the new objective at once; the work assignment named the owner of the Gemini calls only later (steward#8), and the executor's record says its 76 requests were made before that assignment and duplicate the task maker's.
5. That world cost under one dollar. A full run of the benchmark it serves has about 9,716 shots, and paid generators and a judge on top: the same step three times is three times the cost and three answers.

Evidence: the world's public page (https://a-green-hand-jack.github.io/hengworld-worlds/#/w/hw_bd6dcbfd7f6b), its release record `record/decisions/D10-two-description-drafts.json`, the executor's `runs/round2/README.md` and the scorer's `scores/spend/spend.json`.

## What to change

Nothing in HengWorld tells a position that a step which costs money or uses up a quota (generating, scoring or judging with a paid resource) belongs to one function. Change HengWorld's definition (function texts, norms or guides) so that each position knows:

- such a step is done once, by the position that holds the function it belongs to, and its result is published together with the model and the settings used;
- a position that needs that result reads the published one; to check it, it samples, or says why the whole step must be redone, rather than redoing it by default;
- the audit may still rerun such a step to reproduce it, and its record says what it reran and what that cost.

Fact 4 is the one to answer: every position starts on a new objective at once, so a position must know from the start, from the definition itself, which function such a step belongs to, not only once a work assignment arrives; and the other positions make no request to the paid resource for that step before its result is published. The wording is yours.

Say functions, never positions: where a text must say who, use the owner slots (`{{ owners.* }}`). Keep each change small: a sentence or two where the subject already is, not a new section of rules. Write nothing of this world's case into the domain: no model, provider, film, benchmark or price. Change nothing else. If a document describes what you change, change it too, Chinese first with the English copy in the same change.

## Where it goes

A new pull request to `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base `dev`, from a branch of its own. Merging is the maintainer's decision after review.

## How to try it

On `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there, run the repository's six regression suites there, and run a fresh HengWorld world to its release with a small task that uses a paid resource. Give that world an `http` resource for Gemini: upstream `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai`, `credential_env` `GEMINI_API_KEY` (set on the trial machine for `ht-resource run` commands), model `gemini-3.8-flash`, `limits.max_requests` 150. The task, from CrewCut's files (copied there as in the last trials):

- Corpus: Caminandes 3 as CrewCut's published dataset (revision d509bed) gives it, with the pinned master verified by its checksum; the copy of the master only if the pinned file cannot be fetched. No Breakdown rebuild.
- Shot descriptions of all 37 shots with CrewCut's describe step, published with the model and settings used.
- One run: `caminandes3-L1-0000-scr` with the fixed pipeline, smoke profile; c completed with the judge's shot correspondence from those descriptions. Any check of the judge itself stays small (at most 10 shots per control).
- Known from the last world: with this model, CrewCut's describe and judge get an empty reply at their own `max_tokens`; it worked with `reasoning_effort` `none` and the judge's `max_tokens` at least 128.
- Every request to Gemini is recorded with its position and purpose.

The trial world's workers are Claude Code with `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token, with at most 40 executions and 2400 model seconds.

The Gemini key cannot be revoked on its own: as soon as the trial world has reached its release and its records are taken, stop it (`stop`, or `finish`), and leave no command on the trial machine that holds the key.

## What the pull request says

What texts changed and why; the trial world's id and its release; the requests to the paid resource by position and purpose (from the trial world's own records), set against what the steps needed: each paid step made by one position only, any rerun by the audit stated with its count; the limit (150) and whether it was reached: if it was, the count proves nothing and the pull request says so; and how this compares with the 264 of `hw_bd6dcbfd7f6b`.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
# Improve HengWorld from the review of its pull request

The last round made HengWorld: its pull request, #7 to `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian` (branch `hengworld`, base `dev`), and its trial, world `hw_f54caea55d2a` on `trial-machine`, reached a release. The maintainer's review of #7 found the following. This round fixes them in the same pull request.

What the review found:

1. The position name `runner` is a word the kernel already uses. The kernel's time stream records the host side of a world (the driver, claims, sandboxes) as the stream and actor `runner` (`src/hutian/hutian/observe/stream.py`, `src/hutian/hutian/execution/session.py`), and an entry without a role is shown by its actor. So in a HengWorld world an entry such as "world runner driver ended: world-complete" cannot be told apart from the position's own entries. The role-name check in `.agents/tests/test-coordination.py` does not catch it: it counts the names of each definition only in that definition's files. DojoWorld met the same collision and renamed its position to `sparring-partner`.
2. The function texts (`src/hengworld/hengworld/instructions/1-function/*.md.j2`) name other positions (steward, task-maker, runner, scorer, auditor) and repeat what the organization part of the instruction already tells each position: read tiers, who supplies whom, the kernel position a role holds. A function text says what the work is and the standard it is held to; who does what reaches each position through the organization part (DEV 15.3: one kind of information per file). When a world has fewer positions, a function falls to another position and the names written into it are wrong. KaiTianWorld's and DojoWorld's function texts are one paragraph each and name no position; where a norm or guide has to say who, it uses the owner slots (`{{ owners.* }}`).
3. Conditions of the last round were written as rules of the domain. `5-norms/collaboration.md.j2` says that keys for models, generators or judges are not supplied, and the runner's function text says there are no such keys. What a world has comes from its resources, and a world that runs CrewCut's Issue #3 for real will have those keys, so these sentences would mislead its workers. Of the same kind: "Do not paste private code … into issues or messages that are public" in the norms comes from this KaiTianWorld world's public page, not from HengWorld; "the objective names a fallback copy" in the curator's function text comes from the last trial's objective. What one world has, or may not do, reaches it through its objective and its resources.
4. The two CI lines (`docker build … -f src/hengworld/Dockerfile …` in `.github/workflows/candidate.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`) are in the pull request's text, not in its changes: the delivery token could not write `.github/workflows/`. The maintainer has since given it that permission: put them in the pull request.
5. The comment of the organization graph (`assets/hengworld-graph.mmd` and its English copy) says that only task-maker and scorer hold the reference answers; the auditor reads them too, as the instructions correctly say.

Change HengWorld (its definition, instruction texts, graphs and documents, Chinese first with the English copies in the same change) so that the pull request no longer has these, and nothing else. Change nothing that only a worker did. Keep each change small; a renamed position is renamed everywhere it appears (definition, instruction files, both graphs, README and USER in both languages, the per-domain checks).

Where it goes: the same pull request, #7. Push new commits to its branch `hengworld` and update its text; do not open another. Merging is the maintainer's decision after review.

How to try it: as in the last round. On `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there, run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh HengWorld world to its release with the same small task, a short piece of each CrewCut pipeline:

- Breakdown: the dev film Caminandes 3 (2.5 minutes, 37 shots, no dialogue), from the catalogue query to its task packages, compared with the published dataset (cuts, dialogue, hierarchy, task ids), with each difference listed and explained; use the copy of the pinned master only when the pinned file cannot be fetched, and record that;
- Evaluation: one of those tasks run with the fixed pipeline and the placeholder generator, scored up to the delivery check and cut F1.

CrewCut reaches the trial machine as a git bundle copied over ssh, and the other files of the `crewcut` resource the same way. The trial needs no key for a generator, a vision-language model or a judge; what needs one (shot descriptions, the judge, real generators, screening) is not run, and the record says so. The trial world's workers are Claude Code with the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token, with at most 30 executions and 2400 model seconds.

What the pull request says: what was made, what this round changed, and how the new trial ended: the trial world's id, its release, the results of both pieces compared with the last trial's, and what was not run.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages.

comments.body: Layout the kernel reads (same as dojoworld, checked in the HuTian tree): `src/hengworld/hengworld/instructions/1-function/<position>.md.j2` for steward, curator, task-maker, runner, scorer, auditor (one per POSITION, named by position, not function; a position text says which function(s) it carries); `5-norms/collaboration.md.j2` and `5-norms/evidence.md.j2`; `7-guides/<function>.md.j2` named by FUNCTION (direction, corpus, tasks, runs, scoring, audit), only where a recipe is needed (corpus, tasks, audit per architect#2 organization.md). English only, as the other domains. Jinja2 sandbox: only kernel-given variables; the function-owner names are `{{ owners.<function> }}` (e.g. `{{ owners.tasks }}`), never hardcode a position name for another's function in guides; no role conditionals. Function texts are read as plain text without headings is fine (dojoworld style: a paragraph of duties). Please rearrange to this and push; I will not move your files.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
# HengWorld: a world that builds a benchmark and evaluates systems on it

Make a new domain for HuTian: HengWorld (衡, "to weigh"). Building a benchmark is making a scale; evaluating systems is weighing them on it. Its first user is CrewCut, a benchmark of film production by agent systems, but the domain is general: a later world could build, say, a software benchmark with it.

What to make:

- A domain package `hengworld` (command `hengworld`, world id prefix `hw`) beside the five domains under `src/`, equal to them and added the way `DEV.md` says a domain is added: its definition through the `hutian.definitions` entry point, its organization graph in `assets/` in Chinese and English, its system and worker images, its default resources, its place in `install.sh`, the CI workflows and the per-domain checks, and its sections in README and USER, Chinese first with the English copies in the same change.
- The positions, edges, read tiers, functions and release gate are not given here. Design them from the real division of the work of building a benchmark and evaluating systems under one set of rules, and give the reason for each.
- No special cases: nothing in the definition names CrewCut, films or a catalogue. What a benchmark needs comes into a HengWorld world through its objective and the benchmark's own documents.
- The shape of the work, as CrewCut decided for its own pipelines: what needs judgment (finding candidates, reading licences, telling the work from its extras, choosing the file to pin, what to do after a failure, organizing runs) is done by agents; the benchmark's commands are reproducible steps and checks of whether each step succeeded; every decision is recorded as data, so that anyone can reproduce the result from the record without repeating the judgment.
- Keep it small: the positions, their contracts and the release gate make a world, not features.

CrewCut, read only: the `crewcut` resource holds a bare mirror of CrewCut's `dev` (df54b3a), its Issue #3, which says what its two pipelines must do and deliver, the published dataset at revision d509bed, and a copy of the pinned master of Caminandes 3. Read its README.md, `.agents/memory/project/agentic-pipelines.md` and Issue #3. Nothing goes back to CrewCut. CrewCut's open decisions (the vision-language model, the generators and their prices, the judge model, the scale of the official runs, the raters) belong to its maintainer: do not make them.

Where it goes: one pull request to the private repository `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base branch `dev`, which holds HuTian's code. Merging it is the maintainer's decision after review.

How to try it: on `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there, run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh HengWorld world to its release with a small task that covers a short piece of each CrewCut pipeline:

- Breakdown: the dev film Caminandes 3 (2.5 minutes, 37 shots, no dialogue), from the catalogue query to its task packages, compared with the published dataset (cuts, dialogue, hierarchy, task ids), with each difference listed and explained; use the copy of the pinned master only when the pinned file cannot be fetched, and record that;
- Evaluation: one of those tasks run with the fixed pipeline and the placeholder generator, scored up to the delivery check and cut F1.

CrewCut reaches the trial machine as a git bundle copied over ssh, and the other files of the `crewcut` resource the same way. The trial needs no key for a generator, a vision-language model or a judge; what needs one (shot descriptions, the judge, real generators, screening) is not run, and the record says so. The trial world's workers are Claude Code with the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token, with at most 20 executions and 2400 model seconds.

What the pull request says: what was made, and how the trial ended: the trial world's id, its release, the results of both pieces, and what was not run.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
# The kernel's `publish` replaces the host's paths with placeholders

This round changes the kernel every world runs on (`src/hutian/`), not a domain; it is the first round of this world that does. The delivery repository's `dev` (2e787aa) is HuTian's `dev`: it holds the last round's pull request (#8, a paid step is done once), which the maintainer merged, and one small edit made after it. Base this round's work on that `dev`, from a branch of its own.

## What the host showed

1. On 2026-10-21 the six DojoWorld worlds published on `a-green-hand-jack/dojoworld-worlds` (`dw_ba784c2b0024`, `dw_42ca99b35e7d`, `dw_124d9fbd3a8e`, `dw_ed19e197a5df`, `dw_f414f11ec76e`, `dw_31f66e575aa1`) were written to a local directory with `dojoworld publish … --output DIR` at the default depth plus `release_assets`. 52 of the files written hold an absolute path of the host, 135 times in all. Five of the six worlds have some; `dw_124d9fbd3a8e` has none.
2. All 52 are contents of files in a position's repository (`<world>/blobs/<sha>`, the `repo_contents` facet): the status and configuration JSON of the worlds that position ran, which it committed (`runs/<name>/<world id>/status.json`, `status.txt`, `config.json`). The paths are the values of `receipts.directory` (46), `continues_home` (44) and the `read` list of a `world` resource (45). No other file had one: not the snapshot, the stream, the file listing, the release listing or the release files.
3. Every one of them begins with a directory the host holds for the world: its state root (`HUTIAN_HOME`; a world it ran lives under `<state root>/<world id>/worlds/<position>/<child world id>/`), or a state root its configuration gives a `world` resource in `read`. On this host all of them lie under the checkout the worlds were started from. Written with placeholders, they look like `<state root>/dw_…/worlds/<position>/rw_…/receipts` and `<a read state root>/rw_…/receipts`.
4. Public content may hold no absolute path of a machine (a rule of the repository). So these worlds are published without `repo_contents` and `repo_diffs`, and before each publish someone writes the site with `--output` and searches it by hand.
5. What `publish` checks today: every byte of every file it writes is compared with the world's own credential literals, and a hit refuses the publish and removes what was written (`publish.check`; USER 8.2). Nothing is done about the host's paths.
6. Disclosure is a whitelist projection (`observe/redact.py`, `observe/facets.py`): nothing reaches the output unless a granted facet copies it in by name. `repo_contents` copies a file's bytes as they are.
7. The three ways out share one export: `--dry-run` (`publish.dry_run`), `--output` (`publish.build`) and a push, once or with `--watch` (`publish_once` in `cli/main.py`). Each calls `publish.stage` and then `publish.check`.
8. Not every file of an export is written by it: release files and released pages are hard links to the host's copy of the record (`publish._link`, `_pages`), and a push hard-links the staged files into its copy of the data branch (`pages.sync`). DEV 20.2: nothing writes such a file in place, so a link never changes the original.
9. A blob is named by the git sha of its bytes, and `outputs.json` lists each file with that sha and size; a later publish, `--watch` included, reuses the last publish's blobs while a repository has not moved (`_outputs`, `previous`).
10. A PDF, a PNG or a release file (an archive, a video) can hold a path in a compressed or length-bound form. In these six worlds none did.
11. The publish regression tests are in `.agents/tests/test-stream.py` (`PublishOutputTests`, `PublishExportTests` and the publish classes after them). USER 8 and DEV 20 describe publishing.

## What to change

Change the kernel's `publish` so that in every file it writes (a dry run, `--output`, a push and `--watch` alike) the host's paths that belong to the world being published are replaced by readable placeholders, for example `<HUTIAN_HOME>/…`, and the dry run and the result say, for each world, how many were replaced. Which directories count, the placeholder each one gets, and what happens to a file that cannot be rewritten are yours to design; follow the whitelist projection that is already there, and say in the pull request what you chose and why. The world's record on the host stays as it is.

Keep the change small: the kernel's publish, regression tests that fail without the change and pass with it, and USER 8 and DEV 20 where they describe what changes (Chinese first, with the English copy in the same change). No domain definition changes. Write nothing of this case into the kernel: no host, user, directory name or world id.

## Where it goes

A new pull request to `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base `dev`, from a branch of its own. Merging is the maintainer's decision after review.

## How to try it

On `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images there and run the repository's six regression suites there. Then run a fresh world of that version with a tiny task to its verified release: the smallest world that still shows each of its positions doing its part, Claude Code with `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort signed in with the OAuth token, at most 8 executions and 1200 model seconds. Something in that world must hold a host path for the replacement to act on (for instance a file a position commits that names the world's state root): a site with nothing to replace proves nothing.

With that version, run `publish --dry-run` and `publish --output DIR` on the trial world there, and show that the site holds no path of the trial machine's directories that belong to that world (search every file of it), and that the count the dry run reports equals the count in the `--output` result and the number of such paths the world's files held. Push nothing to a public repository from the trial machine.

## What the pull request says

What kernel code changed and why; the regression tests; which directories are replaced and by what, and how files that cannot be rewritten are treated; the trial world's id and its release; the search of the trial site (what was searched for and the counts) and the dry run's count against the result's.

This world is published live on a public page: its time stream, the issues and pull requests between positions, the release list and the turn numbers are public; file contents are not. HuTian's code is private: do not paste it into issues, pull requests or messages, and write no path of this host or of the trial machine there either.
